records.title: Automation
records.description:
Currently, Port can trigger workflows when a change is made in the software catalog, for example, trigger a webhook. This is done with the [changelog listener](https://docs.getport.io/create-self-service-experiences/setup-backend/webhook/examples/changelog-listener). The main problem with the changelog listener is that only one trigger per blueprint can be defined, and each trigger is executed for any change in the catalog, without the ability to define rules for a specific trigger.

With the "Automations" feature, we plan to improve the changelog listener with the following capabilities:

1. The ability to create rules that need to pass in order to trigger automation.

2. Create multiple automations on a specific blueprint

3. Adding many more invocation types when triggering automation, such as executing a Port action, executing a CICD pipeline, and updating entities in the catalog

This will enable scenarios such as:

1. Sending a Slack message when the "Production readiness" scorecards changed from "Gold" to "Silver"

2. Scaling a Cluster according to changes in the CPU usage

3. Updating the "state" property of a service from "Healthy" to "Unhealthy" when a related incident opened in PagerDuty

Of course, these are just examples. The power of this capability is that each organization will be able to create automations based on their developer portal data and needs.

records.user_need: Users want more flexible rules and invocation options for catalog-change-triggered automations.

records.title: Use current user's session to interact with internal systems
records.description:
We'd like to enable identity or user session propagation capabilities, allowing Self-Service Actions (SSAs) triggered within Port to be executed using the context and permissions of the currently logged-in user. When an authenticated user initiates an SSA that interacts with external systems or resources, the action should be performed on behalf of that user, inheriting their identity, role-based access controls (RBAC), and authorized privileges from the same Identity and Access Management (IAM) provider used by Port, which is Okta.

For example, if an employee triggers an SSA to update a ticket in a service management system like Jira, the update should be carried out using that employee's credentials and permissions within Jira, which are derived from the same Okta IAM provider that Port uses for authentication and authorization. Similarly, if an SSA involves provisioning resources in a cloud platform, it should leverage the logged-in user's identity and access rights from Okta to ensure the provisioning adheres to their authorized roles and scopes defined within the shared IAM provider.

By propagating the user's identity and session context from the common Okta IAM provider, we can maintain a consistent access control model across Port and integrated systems, ensuring that actions are performed with the appropriate level of authorization and adhering to the organization's security policies and governance rules defined within the centralized Okta IAM solution.

records.user_need: Ensure that when an action affects an external system, it respects the requester's own access rights and identity as defined in the company's identity provider.
records.suggested_product_action: Support delegated execution that runs actions using the requesting user's identity and permissions from the connected IAM provider (e.g., Okta) rather than a shared service identity.
records.evidence_excerpt: the action should be performed on behalf of that user, inheriting their identity, role-based access controls (RBAC), and authorized privileges

records.title: Confirmation Window for Unsaved Changes in Self-service actions GUI Mode
records.description:
Add a confirmation window in the GUI mode in Self-service action window to prompt users when they attempt to navigate away from the page without saving their changes. Currently, this confirmation prompt exists in JSON mode in Self-service action window, but it is missing in GUI mode, which can lead to accidental data loss.

Rationale:

In the GUI mode, users may accidentally navigate away without saving their changes. A confirmation prompt will help prevent this, ensuring users have the chance to save their work before leaving the page. This feature is especially helpful for complex edits where re-entering data can be time-consuming.

Expected Behavior:

	•	Trigger: When a user tries to navigate away from the page while unsaved changes are present in GUI mode.

	•	Confirmation Prompt: The prompt should ask the user, “Are you sure you want to leave this page without saving changes?” with options to “Stay on Page” or “Leave without Saving.”

	•	Consistency: This behavior should be consistent with the existing confirmation prompt in JSON mode to ensure a seamless user experience across modes.

records.title: Per‑User Impersonation / Delegated Execution for Actions
records.description:
We need Port to support executing self‑service actions as the real user, not as a shared technical account. Today, actions that call tools like GitHub or Jira are executed with an app token, so in those tools every change appears as coming from a generic user. This breaks per‑user traceability required by an external zero‑trust banking audit, is considered a high security risk, and blocks us from safely scaling self‑service to 1,500+ engineers and multiple companies in our group.

Requested capability:

* OAuth2‑based delegated authorization so each Port user can link their own GitHub/Jira account and actions run with their token.

* A consistent “execute as user” model across integrations (GitHub first, then Jira, others later).

* Configurable backend for actions: keep current “machine token” mode, and add a new user‑session/OAuth mode that respects Port RBAC and IdP policies.

This is a blocker for audit compliance, enterprise‑wide adoption, and for comparing Port fairly with other IDPs that already support per‑user execution.

records.user_need: The organization needs every action execution against external tools to be attributable to the real user for compliance and security purposes.
records.suggested_product_action: Support OAuth2-based per-user delegated execution so actions run with the requesting user's own linked credentials instead of a shared service token, while still respecting RBAC.
records.evidence_excerpt: actions that call tools like GitHub or Jira are executed with an app token, so in those tools every change appears as coming from a generic user

records.title: Expose Catalogue Usage Telemetry

When a user (Bob) runs a self-service action via Port an event is fired off to DX saying that Bob did X event. DX looks to see if Bob is eligible for surveying based on the action (event) taken and if valid will send a survey to them personally on teams (MS Bot framework). This gives a very low friction option for Bob to provide feedback they might have otherwise not raised.

So, the user experience might be that Bob accesses the new port dashboard page for the first time and sometime later is pinged on teams saying "Hey we saw you used the ABC dashboard for the first time. Could you let us know what you thought etc..."

Currently we don't have access to data that tells us who has accessed what pages in the catalogue at what time. Could this data/event telemetry be made available?

records.title: Improved Retry Mechanism for Port Synchronization
records.description:
The current retry mechanism in Port does not handle well synchronization failures caused by race conditions and temporary issues. This feature request proposes an enhanced retry system to improve data consistency and reliability with eventual consistency.

1. Automated Re-sync for Specific Blueprints (based on missing realations)

Add support for automated re-sync based on missing relations in blueprint entities.

- Improve the current periodic re-sync feature to support specific blueprints

- Add support for configuring conditional re-sync only if there are errors caused by missing relations

This will ensure eventual consistency for objects with infrequent updates (e.g., re-sync only for k8s namespaces when k8s pod has missing namespace as a relation)

2. Implement Exponential Backoff

- Replace the current retry system with an exponential backoff mechanism

- Gradually increase the time between retry attempts to reduce system load and improve success rates

3. Retry for Relation Sync Issues

- Enable retry attempts specifically for entities created with relation sync issues

- Target scenarios where related entities may not have been imported yet due to timing

Benefits

- More efficient use of system resources during retries

- Higher success rate for entity synchronization

- Automatic resolution of temporary inconsistencies

- Improved data integrity and completeness over time

This feature will enhance Port's ability to maintain consistent and complete data, especially in complex scenarios involving multiple related entities and large-scale imports.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns data source synchronization and blueprint entity relation consistency, not the configuration or execution of self-service actions.
records.short_summary: Users want a more reliable retry mechanism for syncing catalog data when relations between entities are temporarily missing.
records.user_need: Ensure catalog data stays consistent and complete even when related entities are imported out of order or sync fails intermittently.
records.suggested_product_action: Improve data source synchronization retry logic with exponential backoff and relation-aware re-sync
records.evidence_excerpt: The current retry mechanism in Port does not handle well synchronization failures caused by race conditions and temporary issues.

records.title: HashiCorp Vault for Secrets Management in Port Actions/Workflows

The workaround today is to route through a CI system (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.) that handles the Vault key exchange, but this introduces an unwanted dependency for teams using a direct orchestrator pattern where the orchestrator feeds execution feedback back into Port.

Requested Capability:

Native support for HashiCorp Vault as a secrets backend for Port Actions/Workflows — allowing Port to resolve secrets at runtime from Vault rather than storing them locally.

Use Case:

Customer: Sophos (via Nuno Pinto)

Trigger: Self-Service Action → direct webhook/orchestrator call requiring authenticated API keys

Constraint: Infosec policy mandates all secrets stored in HashiCorp Vault only

Current gap: No native Vault secrets resolution; CI workaround not viable for their direct-trigger architecture

records.user_need: Ensure sensitive credentials remain solely in the organization's Vault while still allowing Actions to authenticate to external systems at runtime.

records.title: RBAC for Port Usage Dashboard

Current behavior

The Usage Dashboard is automatically visible to all Org Admins in Pro & Enterprise orgs. [Usage dashboard announcement]

This access cannot be changed or restricted today; all Org Admins always see it.

Problem

Usage and billing‑related data is sensitive. Organizations want least‑privilege access and the ability to limit visibility to a small group (e.g., platform owners, FinOps, auditors), not all Org Admins. 

Requested change

Add RBAC controls for the Usage Dashboard

Configure who can view it by:

Roles

Specific users

Teams

This should be similar in spirit to existing page permissions (view/edit by roles/users/teams). 

Configurable default behavior

Keep current default (all Org Admins) for backward compatibility, but allow organizations to override it (e.g., restrict to selected roles/users/teams)

Impact

Better alignment with least‑privilege and compliance requirements.

Consistent RBAC story across Port (catalog pages, dashboards, and platform‑level features like Usage Dashboard).

records.title: Support Service Account Credentials for Signing Port Execution Agent Messages
records.description:
Currently, the Port Execution Agent verifies incoming events by validating the X-Port-Signature header, which is signed using the organization-level Client Secret. This means that even when a service account is configured as the agent's credentials, the signature verification still relies on the org-level secret — not the service account credentials.

This creates a security concern for customers with strict internal security standards, who prefer to use service account credentials to limit blast radius in case of a credential leak, following the principle of least privilege.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns how Port signs and verifies execution agent messages for self-service actions, a security mechanism directly tied to action invocation.
records.short_summary: Message signing for the execution agent uses the org-wide secret instead of the configured service account, increasing security exposure if the org secret leaks.
records.user_need: Limit the blast radius of a credential leak by having message signing scoped to the specific service account rather than the whole organization.
records.suggested_product_action: Support signing execution agent messages using service account credentials instead of the organization-level client secret

records.title: Enhance `sendRawDataExamples` options for faster data source mapping
records.description:
For some kinds available in integration, the API responses can vary greatly depending on certain conditions. As a concrete example, in the github integration, the `branch` kind only contains properties like `.branch.commit.commit.author` when the branch is the default branch of a given repository, and in my mapping I set the query to `.branch.name == .repository.default_branch` to ensure I have access to that value.

What I'm currently finding is that the sendRawDataExamples option in integrations does not respect this query setting, so the ~5 examples retained from the api call might not even contain a valid api response (as in, one that passes the check in `query`). 

I have a few varied suggestions here:

- Allow `sendRawDataExamples` to respect the given query in a mapping.

- Allow `sendRawDataExamples` to have it's own query for stricter or looser example api responses.

- Allow independent resync of `sendRawDataExamples` separate from a resync of the data source.

Giving builders the ability to have stronger control over the examples defined in the data source view would significantly improve iteration time when dealing with complex mappings across multiple data sources.
records.relevance_reason: This feedback concerns data source integration mapping and sendRawDataExamples behavior, which is a catalog/data ingestion feature, not self-service Actions configuration.

The approval request should include the relevant context (requester, action, parameters) so the approver can make an informed decision without leaving Slack.

For an IDP platform focused on developer experience, inline approval actions in Slack are table stakes. Requiring approvers to leave Slack and navigate to Port adds friction, slows down approval cycles, and reduces adoption of self-service workflows. This is a foundational expectation for any approvals feature.

Displays approval requests in Slack with a structured list of pending items and inline action buttons to approve or reject without leaving the conversation.

Sawmills

An example from a small startup demonstrating that inline Slack action buttons are achievable even at an early stage — reinforcing that this is an expected baseline, not a complex feature.

records.title: Configurable Retry Status Codes for Integrations
records.description:
Summary: 

- Allow users to configure which HTTP status codes trigger automatic retries via spec.yaml, without modifying integration source code.

Background: 

- The Ocean framework's RetryConfig class already supports additional_retry_status_codes, but this is not exposed to users. All integrations that use custom retry codes (PagerDuty, Sentry, GitHub, etc.) have them hardcoded in the client code. 

- Default retryable status codes: 400, 401, 429, 502, 503, 504

Problem: 

- Different third-party APIs have varying reliability characteristics. Some APIs intermittently return 500 or other error codes that would benefit from retry logic. Users currently cannot configure this without forking and maintaining a custom version of the integration.

Proposed Solution: 

- Add an optional additionalRetryStatusCodes configuration to spec.yaml.

Benefits

- Users can adapt to their specific API behavior without code changes

- Fully backward compatible as an optional configuration

- Leverages existing RetryConfig infrastructure

Use Cases

- GitLab self-hosted instances returning intermittent 500 errors under load

- APIs behind flaky proxies returning frequent 502/503 errors

- Cloud provider APIs with known transient 500 error patterns

Related Code

- port_ocean/helpers/retry.py - RetryConfig class

- port_ocean/helpers/async_client.py - OceanAsyncClient

- integrations/pagerduty/clients/pagerduty.py (lines 31-38) - example hardcoded implementation
records.relevance_reason: This concerns retry configuration for Ocean data-source integrations that sync catalog data, not self-service Action execution or configuration.
records.short_summary: Users cannot configure which HTTP error codes trigger automatic retries for Ocean data-source integrations without forking the code.
records.user_need: The ability to tune retry behavior for third-party API integrations that have varying reliability.
records.suggested_product_action: Expose additionalRetryStatusCodes configuration in spec.yaml for Ocean integrations
records.evidence_excerpt: Users currently cannot configure this without forking and maintaining a custom version of the integration.

records.title: MCP Action Access Controls - Restrict Actions by Invocation Source

Adding an invocation source control at the action level in Port, allowing admins to configure which channels an action can be triggered from would allow teams to enforce that sensitive actions (e.g., prod deploys, destructive operations) cannot be triggered via MCP, without needing to rely on external configuration in the AI client (e.g., Claude system prompt restrictions).

records.title: Configurable automatic execution of self-service actions from Slack

Add a configuration option that allows admins to control whether self-service actions triggered via the Slack app can be:

Executed automatically from Slack once all required parameters are collected, or

Value / Impact

Reduces context switching for developers and on-call engineers who want to complete workflows entirely within Slack.

Preserves safety by making automatic execution opt-in and configurable by platform/admin teams.

Aligns Slack app behavior with customers’ expectations for fully chat-native self-service while keeping the current secure default.

records.title: “Execute” Button on the First Step of the Input Window
records.description:
We would like to have an “Execute” button to the first step of the Self-service action with many steps input window. This button will allow users to initiate the action immediately if they do not need to modify any fields in subsequent steps.

Rationale:

The first step contains all required fields for the action. For users who do not wish to change any optional fields in the following steps, this “Execute” button would allow them to bypass unnecessary navigation through all steps just to initiate the action at the end. This feature will improve user efficiency and reduce friction in workflows where default settings are frequently used.

Expected Behavior:

	•	Location: The “Execute” button should appear prominently on the first step of the input form.

	•	Functionality: If clicked, the button should validate all required fields in the first step, initiate the action

	•	Fallback: If any required fields are missing or incorrect, the button should provide feedback to the user, prompting them to complete or correct those fields.

Benefits:

	•	Saves time for users who don’t need to modify optional fields.

	•	Reduces the number of interactions needed for common use cases.

	•	Enhances overall user experience by streamlining the workflow.

records.title: Control which Port Execution Agent deployment process which message with polling streamer
records.description:
With Port Execution Agent that use polling streamer  (https://docs.port.io/actions-and-automations/setup-backend/webhook/port-execution-agent/usage#polling-streamer), messages are acknowledged before processing and cannot be claimed by another agent once fetched.

This allows multiple agents to run in parallel without conflicts, but requires using the same filtering logic across all agents to avoid unintended filtering.

You cannot control which agent processes which message at the moment.

Suggested solution:

Set and optional "cluster identifier" that is evaluated when executing the run. The poller will send its "cluster identifier", only matching runs will be fetched.

records.short_summary: Users can only configure the agent's payload mapping via raw config files or install-time settings, not through the UI.
records.user_need: A way to view and edit the payload mapping configuration for an execution agent directly in the UI, similar to other integrations.
records.suggested_product_action: Provide a UI editor for configuring and updating the execution agent's payload mapping without requiring reinstallation.
records.evidence_excerpt: Currently, you can only update the mapping config directly at the agent/provide the mapping when you install it.

records.title: Runs - displaying the payload
records.description: The payload of a specific run is now displayed in Port’s specific run page and audit log under the “Payload” property.
records.relevance_reason: This describes viewing the invocation payload for a specific Action run, which is part of Run observability.
records.short_summary: Port now shows the payload used for a run directly on the run page and audit log.
records.user_need: Wants to see exactly what data was sent when a specific action run was triggered.
records.suggested_product_action: Display the invocation payload on the run details page and audit log
records.evidence_excerpt: The payload of a specific run is now displayed in Port’s specific run page and audit log under the “Payload” property.

records.title: Disallow saving actions with no execute permissions
records.description:
Currently, execute permissions can be removed entirely, which allows an action to be saved with no execute permissions at all. We need a product safeguard to prevent this by either:

Disallowing actions from being saved without any execute permissions, or

Automatically retaining the Admin role as a default execute permission.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns configuring execute permissions on self-service actions and preventing an invalid permission state from being saved.
records.short_summary: Actions can be saved with no one able to execute them because all execute permissions can be removed without warning.
records.user_need: Ensure an action always retains at least one valid execute permission so it cannot become unusable.
records.suggested_product_action: Prevent saving an action configuration that has no execute permissions, or default to retaining an admin execute permission.
records.evidence_excerpt: execute permissions can be removed entirely, which allows an action to be saved with no execute permissions at all

records.title: Manual approval for self-service actions
records.description:
Admins can define an approval step on chosen self-service actions.

 This capability will allow setting guardrails on sensitive actions, while still allowing users to perform actions in a self-service manner.

 Actions with an approval step will be created in “waiting for approval” status, the approving party will be notified so they can approve or decline the action.

 See [how to configure an approval step](https://docs.getport.io/self-service-actions/self-service-actions-deep-dive/#manual-approval)
records.relevance_reason: This describes configuring approval workflows on self-service actions, which is core Action Configuration.
records.short_summary: Admins can now require approval before a sensitive self-service action runs, with the requester's action held pending until an approver decides.
records.user_need: Platform admins need a way to add guardrails so sensitive actions require sign-off before execution while still keeping the process self-service.
records.suggested_product_action: Provide configurable approval steps for self-service actions, including approver notification and waiting-for-approval status.
records.evidence_excerpt: Admins can define an approval step on chosen self-service actions.

records.title: Option to Exclude Hidden Inputs from SSA Manual-Approval Emails
records.description:
Hidden SSA inputs (configured via visibility rules) are still included in the default manual-approval email by design, to give approvers full context.

Request

Add a configuration option to exclude hidden inputs from the default approval email, while keeping them in the submitted payload for backend processing. For example, an action-level flag like excludeHiddenInputsFromApprovalEmail: true (default false to preserve current behavior).

Value

Reduces noise in approval emails (especially large JSON/object inputs).

Lets teams keep technical/auxiliary fields hidden from both requesters and approvers, without losing them from the action payload.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns configuring what information appears in manual-approval emails for self-service actions.
records.short_summary: Approval emails always show hidden form fields, cluttering the message even when those fields should stay out of view.
records.user_need: The action builder wants to keep certain technical or auxiliary fields hidden from approvers' emails while still sending them to the backend.
records.suggested_product_action: Add a configuration option to exclude hidden inputs from approval notification emails while retaining them in the submitted payload.
records.evidence_excerpt: Add a configuration option to exclude hidden inputs from the default approval email, while keeping them in the submitted payload for backend processing.

records.title: Bypass Self-Service Approval Need if submitter is an approver
records.description:
My team approves certain self-service actions. Me and my team also use the same self-service actions for our own day-to-day work at times. When we submit one of these requests we approve our own requests. While some requests might warrant a separate approver, even on the same team, in our case we don't. We simply need the self-service action to execute, but we have to approve our own request, which is just extra work.

Today there is a "General access" section at the bottom of the Approvers section of the Edit action window. There is a toggle for Admins, so admins do not need approval. My Feature Request is to possibly rename the "General access" heading because this doesn't seem intuitive. Instead, name it something like "Approval Bypass". Keep Admins and add a new toggle like "Approvers". When enabled, if a requestor is a named approver or in an approver group then requests by that user would not need to be approved.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns configuring approval policies for self-service actions, specifically bypassing approval requirements.
records.short_summary: Approvers who submit their own requests must approve themselves, creating unnecessary extra work.
records.user_need: Approvers want their own self-service requests to skip the approval step when they are also an eligible approver.
records.suggested_product_action: Add an approval-bypass toggle that lets requests from named approvers or approver groups auto-approve without requiring self-approval.
records.evidence_excerpt: When we submit one of these requests we approve our own requests

records.title: Allow non-admins to create and/or edit self-service actions
records.description:
I want to allow some users to be able to create self-service actions in our STG environment without giving them full Admin access.

Alternatively, if we had RBAC over who can EDIT self-service actions then I could create a self-service action that creates a "shell" self-service action for users with the proper RBAC on it that would grant them edit access.
records.relevance_reason: This is specifically about controlling who can create or edit self-service action definitions, which is core to Port Actions administration.
records.short_summary: Admins cannot grant limited users permission to create or edit self-service actions without giving them full admin rights.
records.user_need: The user needs a way to delegate action-authoring privileges to specific team members without exposing them to full administrative control.
records.suggested_product_action: Introduce role-based access control for creating and editing self-service action definitions independent of full admin permissions.
records.evidence_excerpt: I want to allow some users to be able to create self-service actions in our STG environment without giving them full Admin access.

records.title: Action run dashboard/homepage widget
records.description:
A dashboard/homepage widget that displays the runs of a specific self-service action.

The widget will display as columns the general details of each run (ID, status, start, end) and also the specific inputs of the action inputted by the user who executed it.
records.relevance_reason: Requests a widget to view and monitor self-service action run history and details, which is core Action execution monitoring.
records.short_summary: Users want a dashboard widget that shows the run history and input details for a specific self-service action.
records.user_need: To monitor and review past runs of an action, including their status and the inputs used, directly from a dashboard without navigating elsewhere.
records.suggested_product_action: Provide a dashboard widget that lists action runs with status, timestamps, and submitted input values for a chosen action.
records.evidence_excerpt: A dashboard/homepage widget that displays the runs of a specific self-service action.

records.title: Dynamic run name for an action run
records.description: I would like a new tab and property in the 'Action Runs' audit page, which is a dynamic title that can be created from the inputs and entity properties.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns the Action Runs audit page and how runs are identified there, which is part of monitoring and debugging action executions.
records.short_summary: Users cannot give action runs a dynamic, meaningful name derived from inputs or entity properties in the run history view.
records.user_need: The user wants to be able to easily identify and distinguish specific action runs in the audit history by a meaningful, context-derived name.
records.suggested_product_action: Add a configurable dynamic run name property, generated from inputs and entity properties, displayed in the Action Runs audit view.
records.evidence_excerpt: a dynamic title that can be created from the inputs and entity properties

records.title: Execute another self-service action run with the similar inputs
records.description:
Today, after a run is completed, it is possible to run it again with the "Re-run" button, which opens the execution form with the run's inputs that can be edited.

We want the ability to execute another run with the same inputs as an existing run, while it is in progress.

We might need to change the wording from "Re-run" as it can be thought as if the current run would be cancelled.

And, to prevent running the same inputs twice by mistake, we might want to open a confirmation dialog.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns triggering another run of a self-service action with similar inputs, which is an Action execution lifecycle capability.
records.short_summary: Users cannot start a new run with the same inputs as an in-progress run without waiting for it to finish, and the current 'Re-run' wording risks confusion about cancelling the active run.
records.user_need: The user wants to launch another run with the same inputs as an existing run while that run is still in progress, without accidentally cancelling it or duplicating it by mistake.
records.suggested_product_action: Enable starting a duplicate run with the same inputs while the original run is still in progress, with clearer labeling and a confirmation step to prevent accidental duplicate execution.
records.evidence_excerpt: We want the ability to execute another run with the same inputs as an existing run, while it is in progress.

records.title: Support Multi-Dimensional Arrays
records.description:
Currently Port supports Arrays of Strings, Numbers, and Objects. This Arrays are limited to one dimension only.

It could be useful to support multi-dimensional Arrays as well.

For example, a 2-dimensional Array of Strings could be used to contain tables with multiple rows and columns.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns Port's data model / property types (arrays), not the configuration, execution or approval of self-service Actions.
records.short_summary: The user wants the catalog data model to support multi-dimensional arrays for storing tabular data.
records.user_need: The user wants to represent table-like data with rows and columns in a single property.
records.suggested_product_action: Support multi-dimensional array property types in the data model
records.evidence_excerpt: It could be useful to support multi-dimensional Arrays as well.

records.title: Automations | Show warning incase automation will be triggered over x times a day
records.description:
In case an automation which is about to be created is going to be triggered a lot of times, a warning for the customer is important, since it might cause a lot of pipelines and jobs to run, inflicting high costs.

Using the audit log history, an estimation can be provided for the trigger count.
records.relevance_reason: This concerns general Automations (event-triggered workflows) rather than Port self-service Actions configuration, running, approving or debugging.
records.short_summary: Users want a warning before creating an automation that could trigger excessively often and drive up costs.
records.user_need: Understand the likely trigger frequency of a new automation before enabling it to avoid unexpected costs.
records.suggested_product_action: Provide a pre-creation warning estimating automation trigger frequency based on audit log history.
records.evidence_excerpt: a warning for the customer is important, since it might cause a lot of pipelines and jobs to run, inflicting high costs
